title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 22-24). The data are a lattice 𝓕 of 'figures' with order ≤ (sub-figure), join ∨, meet ∧ and empty figure ∅. Inside it sits a set M of elementary figures. Each F ∈ 𝓕 has a set of constituents F̃ ⊂ M, and F = sup_{X∈F̃} X. On M there is a second order ≪. Under axioms C4 and C6, p.22 shows that ≤ and ≪ coincide on each F̃. It also defines the 'shadow' map (129), M ↪ 𝒫(M), X ↦ Omb(X) = {Y ∈ M | Y ≪ X}. This map is injective and turns ≪ into inclusion. The 'multi-shadow' Multomb(F) is the image of F̃ under Omb. It is a figure in 𝒫(M) whose sub-figures are the subsets closed (downward) for inclusion. In effect Multomb replaces a geometric figure by a combinatorial model: a poset of shadows, like a face poset or stratification poset.

Proposition. For F, G ∈ 𝓕 the following are equivalent:
(i) F ≤ G;
(i bis) F̃ ⊂ G̃;
(ii) Multomb(F) ≤ Multomb(G), i.e. Multomb(F) is a sub-figure of Multomb(G);
(ii bis) Multomb(F) ⊂ Multomb(G).

Proof.
- (i)⇔(i bis) is recalled 'pour mémoire'. ⇒ is trivial. ⇐ holds because F = sup F̃ and G = sup G̃.
- (i bis)⇔(ii bis) follows from the injectivity of (129).
- (ii)⇒(ii bis) is tautological.
- For (ii bis)⇒(ii), one must show that Multomb(F) is closed (a down-set for inclusion) in Multomb(G). Since F̃ ⊂ G̃ and hence F ≤ G, F̃ is closed in G̃ for ≤ (= ≪ there).

Corollary. Let F, G be compatible (F ≭ G, notation of p.22). Then Multomb(F) and Multomb(G) are compatible, and:
- Multomb(F∨G) = Multomb(F) ∪ Multomb(G);
- Multomb(F∧G) = Multomb(F) ∩ Multomb(G).
The proof is on the next page: the constituents of F∨G are F̃ ∪ G̃, in which F̃ and G̃ are closed, and the constituents of F∧G are F̃ ∩ G̃.

A crossed-out remark restates condition (ii): F̃ and G̃ are closed in F̃ ∪ G̃ for ≪, which is induced by ⊂ in 𝒫(M).

Purpose. The page establishes that F ↦ Multomb(F) is an order embedding of the figures into 'combinatorial' figures of 𝒫(M), and a lattice morphism on compatible pairs. This is a Birkhoff-type representation of figures by down-sets of their elementary constituents, serving the axiomatic tame-topology ('analysis situs') programme of 1986.
errors: The transcription's 'dense[?]' in the last line of the proof is almost certainly 'fermé'/'fermée' (closed for the order, i.e. down-closed). Density would not give what is needed. As written in the transcription the argument would be wrong.

The step 'F̃ ⊂ G̃ ⇒ F̃ closed in G̃' is called trivial. It relies on F̃ being the down-set M_{≤F} and on ≤ = ≪ on G̃ (Corollary 1, p.22), which together give down-closure for ≪. This is fine but implicit.
In the Corollary, F, G should range over 𝓕 (figures), not M; the handwriting is ambiguous.

The compatibility hypothesis is needed. The next page notes that the converse (compatibility of the Multomb's implies compatibility of F and G) fails in general, with a counterexample of two points and a vaguely stated regularity condition left as 'vérifier plus tard'.

ideas.what: Representation of a figure by the set of 'shadows' Omb(X) = {Y ≪ X} of its constituents (Multomb), giving an order embedding F ↦ Multomb(F) into down-closed families in 𝒫(M).
ideas.modern_name: Birkhoff/Priestley-type representation of a lattice by down-sets of (join-)irreducibles; face poset / stratification poset with Alexandrov topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (1937), Stone/Priestley; Alexandrov (1937) for poset topologies; face posets in PL topology
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished 1986 'Analysis situs' manuscripts; the tame-topology programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5-6, but not this formalism

ideas.what: Multomb preserves joins and meets of compatible figures (union and intersection of shadow families).
ideas.modern_name: Lattice homomorphism on compatible pairs / sublattice embedding into down-set lattice

missed.claim: The page is a routine order-theoretic step in Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic 'analysis situs' (figures, constituents, shadows). Its only interest is documentary: it shows a combinatorial 'shadow poset' model of tame figures, which anticipates the role of stratification posets in later tame/o-minimal and stratified homotopy theory. There is no new theorem.
missed.quote: Multomb(F∨G) = Multomb(F) ∪ Multomb(G), Multomb(F∧G) = Multomb(F) ∩ Multomb(G)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of historical interest for reconstructing Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics of tame topology. Mathematically it is standard lattice theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is an elementary representation result (a Birkhoff-type embedding into down-sets), correct and routine. Its interest lies only in documenting the unpublished 1986 tame-topology axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: '(ii) ... i.e. Multomb(F) est mono-figé[?] dans Multomb(G)' should read '... i.e. Multomb(F) est une sous-figure de Multomb(G)'.
'{+pour ensembles[?]+}' is more likely 'pour mémoire' (with '(⇒ trivial, ⇐ car ...)').
'par l'injectivité de (4.3.9)[?]' should be 'par l'injectivité de (129)' (the map M ↪ 𝒫(M) of p.22).
'est fermé[?] dans Multomb G pour l'inclusion' should be 'est fermée dans Multomb G pour l'inclusion'.
'F̃ est {+dense[?]+} dans G̃' is almost certainly 'F̃ est fermé dans G̃' (closed/down-closed).
In the Corollary, 'F ∉ G' / 'F ≰ G' should be 'F ≭ G' (compatible), and '(Multomb(F) ≰ Multomb(G))' should be 'Multomb(F) ≭ Multomb(G)'.
'On (ii bis) est impliqué par (ii) (tautologique)' should be 'Or (ii bis) est impliqué par (ii) (tautologique)'.
